Bazı para transferlerinin haber karşılığı ödeme olabileceği değerlendirilirken, para hareketleri şüpheli bulunduğu kaydedildi.

articles.title: Mazda MX-5 drops 181bhp 2.0-litre engine in UK
articles.title_tr: Mazda MX-5 drops 181bhp 2.0-litre engine in UK
articles.summary:
Drop-top will remain on sale with a 1.5-litre engine, but you'll have to move quickly to get the 2.0

The range-topping 2.0-litre version of the Mazda MX-5 has been axed in the UK, Autocar can reveal.
Several dealers have confirmed to Autocar that the long-running convertible is no longer available to order with the 181bhp 2.0-litre powerplant. Posts on the Mazda MX-5 Owners’ Club have reported similarly.
This means the MX-5 can now be had with only the 130bhp 1.5-litre. This set-up also forgoes a limited-slip differential, a feature that adds to the model’s appeal as a driver’s car.
A spokesperson for Mazda UK told Autocar: “The 2.0-litre was dropped from the European markets in 2024 due to changing emissions regulations. However, due to different derogation timings in the UK, we were able to continue with an extended sales period. This period has now ended and we will cease sales of the 2.0-litre Mazda MX-5 in the UK once the existing stock has been sold.
“We have sufficient stock of 2.0-litre models to meet anticipated customer demand until around January 2027, while the 1.5-litre Mazda MX-5 will continue to be available in the UK.
“The 1.5-litre engine remains at the heart of the MX-5. The current-generation MX-5 was originally developed around this engine, with its light weight, responsive and accessible performance perfectly reflecting [Mazda’s philosophy of] Jinba Ittai [‘horse and rider’].
“The continuation of the 1.5-litre ensures customers can continue to enjoy the lightweight, engaging and fun-to-drive experience that has defined the Mazda MX-5 for more than 35 years and continues to win awards as one of the best driving cars on the road today.”
Offering only a lower-polluting engine will also help Mazda to comply with the UK’s zero emissions vehicle (ZEV) mandate. The 2.0-litre emits 153g/km compared with the 140g/km put out by the 1.5. Although the ZEV mandate concerns the nation’s EV sales, it also rewards manufacturers for making big cuts to their fleets’ emissions.
The Japanese-market 1.5 was recently updated to raise its outputs to 134bhp and 114lb ft – mild increases of 4bhp and 3lb ft – while also reducing its fuel consumption. The UK is expected to receive this upgrade in due course. 
It remains to be seen how much longer Mazda can continue to sell the MX-5 in the UK. Although it is effectively Mazda’s halo model, it is now more than a decade old and sales have dwindled in recent years, falling from around 4000 in 2019 to roughly 1500 in the years thereafter.
Autocar this year awarded the 2.0-litre MX-5 a rare five-star rating in its road test, dubbing it the “definitive sports car”.

articles.title_tr: The Lord Of The Rings Extended Trilogy Is Massively Discounted Just After Surprise Game Re-Release
articles.summary:
If the recent re-release of The Lord of the Rings: War in the North got you excited about the fantasy franchise and looking for more, Amazon currently has a great deal going for the Peter Jackson movies. 



The retailer is selling a digital copy of the three-movie extended-edition bundle for just $15. It normally goes for $45, so this is quite a deal, at least if you're OK owning the movies digitally. 




https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zckJCxYxn1g




2026 is the 25th anniversary of the films, as The Fellowship of the Ring debuted in 2001. The sequels The Two Towers and The Return of the King followed in 2002 and 2003, respectively. They were all big hits critically and commercially.



Return of the King, for its part, swept at the Oscars in 2004, winning all 11 of the awards it was nominated for, including Best Picture and Best Director for Jackson. There are more The Lord of the Rings movies now in the works, including The Hunt for Gollum in 2027. 



As for the game series, recent entries like The Lord of the Rings: Gollum and Tales of the Shire left a lot to be desired.  There are new games now in the works, including a "deeply immersive" game from Kingdom Come studio Warhorse. Additionally, Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is said to be working on its own The Lord of the Rings game. There will also be more re-releases of "classic" The Lord of the Rings games coming up.
